firmwareAttestation.story: firmware attestation is the device's proof-of-liveness analog — a signed reading is only as alive as the firmware that produced it

lifecycle.story: Node #7 was pulled from the riverbank after flood damage and formally decommissioned. Its device DIDz is terminal: the standing grants that let it write telemetry into Nightowl's data plane are revoked, and a 'fresh' reading signed by this node must be rejected — exactly the retained-signal fraud the convention receiver villain probes.
kernelExpectations: decommissioning revokes the device's standing grants recursively — a dead sensor must not keep authority
no new credential may be issued by or about this device after the terminal status flips
a retained pre-decommission reading replayed as 'fresh' fails the freshness check — same rule as VILLAIN--convention-receiver--retained-signal-presented-as-fresh-proof
the device's history stays readable as a terminal archive; the vault never deletes provenance
